workflows.name: Delay, EOT & Weather Event Documentation for Claims
workflows.notes: Documented financial outcomes: $100k AUD (Akaysha Energy), $75k USD avoided liquidated damages (Barnhill), 20 additional weather days validated (Origin Energy).

steps.description: A weather event or other qualifying delay event occurs on site, preventing or significantly impeding work on critical-path activities.
Site superintendent or PM logs the event in the daily site diary and weather log, noting the start/end time of the stoppage and the activities affected.
PM or planner identifies the relevant Evercam cameras and time windows covering the affected work areas for the duration of the event.
Evercam recordings reviewed and footage clips extracted showing site conditions during the event — idle plant, workers sheltering, standing water, absence of productive activity.
Compare/snapshot tool used to generate before-and-after images showing site conditions immediately before and during (or after) the event.
Evercam built-in weather report for the site exported for the relevant period — capturing rainfall, wind speed, and temperature data to corroborate visual evidence.
Footage clips, weather report, and programme analysis compiled into a formal change order or EOT package alongside the contract's baseline weather allowance comparison.
Package submitted to the owner or their PM/QS representative.
Owner reviews the package — the visual evidence reduces or eliminates the owner's ability to dispute that the event occurred or caused a genuine stoppage.
Change order or EOT approved (or parties enter negotiation with a shared factual basis established by the footage). Approved adjustment recorded in the contract.

workflows.trigger: A weather event or other external disruption causes a stoppage to a critical-path activity, and the contractor believes they are entitled to additional time and/or cost compensation.
workflows.activity: Assembling and packaging documented visual and meteorological evidence that links specific adverse conditions to specific periods of demonstrable site inactivity — for submission as a formal EOT or prolongation claim.

evidence.quote: Evercam footage and the weather report were used together to support the change order — the footage showed idle equipment and standing water, and the weather report confirmed the rainfall. The owner approved the claim without dispute.

Mike needed a local recording of Sunday, July 13th at 14:00 to 14:30 to show extreme weather — this ended up helping them go back to the subcontractor on rework of roof damage and internally to upper management on why a schedule change was needed due to weather damage.
Flood caused by council's pipes rather than contractor. Added insurance company to camera and were able to establish responsibility. Resolved in 30 minutes rather than 3 days.

workflows.conclusion: The change order or EOT claim package is submitted. Owner reviews and claim is approved, negotiated, or disputed with a shared factual basis established by footage.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam camera recordings and the built-in weather report tool are used together to produce a corroborated visual and meteorological record of site conditions during adverse weather events or other delay-causing circumstances.

workflows.name: Delivery Verification & Material Quantity Reconciliation
workflows.notes: Operates at two frequencies: (a) routine/periodic reconciliation — a daily or weekly check (GMC Utilities model); (b) triggered investigation.

steps.description: A delivery invoice, docket bundle, or day-work sheet received from a supplier or haulier claiming payment for a number of deliveries or material volumes.
Site manager, QS, or logistics coordinator reviews the claimed delivery count or volume and identifies a discrepancy.
Gate Report accessed and filtered by the relevant date range, gate, and vendor/vehicle category to produce a log of all vehicle entry events for the disputed period.
Gate Report vehicle count compared against the invoiced delivery count — discrepancies noted and documented.
For deliveries where load confirmation is needed, camera recordings at the gate or delivery zone reviewed to visually confirm vehicle load status and content.
For plant and equipment hire disputes, recordings of the relevant work zone reviewed to confirm that plant was on site and operating for the claimed hours.
Discrepancy evidence (Gate Report export + relevant footage clips) compiled and presented to the supplier or subcontractor.
Supplier either confirms the error and issues a corrected invoice, or disputes the Gate Report data. In most evidenced cases, Gate Report data accepted as definitive.
Corrected invoice approved and adjustment recorded in the cost management system.
Gate Report and footage archive retained as part of the project's payment audit trail.

workflows.trigger: A supplier or haulier submits a delivery invoice claiming quantities the site team believes are inconsistent with what was actually received — or a routine reconciliation at month-end reveals a discrepancy.
workflows.activity: Cross-referencing Gate Report vehicle entry/exit logs and camera recordings against paper delivery dockets and supplier invoices.

evidence.quote: We manage to save €100k in contractor over-charges.
evidence.source: Glenveagh [Compliance #56] — machine hire verification using Gate Report

evidence.quote: Subcontractors claimed that they had delivered tables to site. We were able to see that they did not deliver any tables.
Reports on productivity — how many trucks come into the site, any missing dockets. Any invoices too high.
evidence.source: GMC Utilities [Compliance #53] — Gate Report as daily operational reconciliation tool

workflows.conclusion: Delivery record verified and invoice approved, adjusted, or rejected based on the camera and Gate Report evidence.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam's Gate Report ANPR system provides the primary data layer — automatically logging all vehicle entries and exits, enabling cross-reference of actual delivery counts against paper dockets and supplier invoices.

workflows.name: Dispute Resolution — Legal Evidence Retrieval & Formal Claims
workflows.notes: Represents the formal end-state of multiple other dispute workflows — Workers' Compensation (Workflow 12), Variation Claims (Workflow 17), and Delivery Verification (Workflow 18) all feed into this workflow when they escalate.

steps.description: A dispute that has not resolved through negotiation or mediation is formally escalated — legal proceedings commenced, or a formal insurance claim requiring legal support is filed.
Legal counsel or claims consultant identifies that Evercam footage from the relevant time period is potentially material evidence and issues a formal evidence preservation request.
Evercam support team notified of the legal hold requirement — footage for the relevant cameras, time windows, and dates flagged for preservation and protected from overwrite.
Relevant footage identified: cloud recordings accessed for standard time windows; local recording extraction requested for extended periods or higher-resolution requirements.
Evercam support extracts the local high-frame-rate recordings and provides them in a format suitable for legal review.
Footage reviewed by the legal team and the client — key clips identified and indexed by event, timestamp, and relevance to the claim.
Chain-of-custody record established — documenting who accessed, extracted, and handled the footage and when.
Where footage authenticity may be challenged, Evercam may be asked to provide a technical witness statement confirming the recording system's integrity and timestamp accuracy.
Footage evidence package formally disclosed to the opposing party's legal representatives in accordance with applicable disclosure rules.
Footage presented at adjudication, arbitration, or trial — either resolving the matter or forming part of the evidence bundle.
Proceedings conclude. Footage archive retained for the applicable statutory period.

workflows.trigger: A construction dispute fails to resolve through negotiation and escalates to formal legal or adjudication proceedings. Legal counsel is engaged and a formal evidence package must be assembled.
workflows.activity: Retrieving, preserving, and formally packaging Evercam footage and associated metadata as admissible evidence for use in legal proceedings.

evidence.quote: Evercam footage was formally disclosed as part of the evidence bundle in a formal adjudication proceeding — the adjudicator referenced the footage in their decision, finding in favour of the main contractor on a disputed variation claim.

Trevor brought the subby into his office and showed him a video of what happened (on Evercam), after which he returned the €70k. Trevor explained that if the video was not produced, the subby was willing to go to court.
evidence.source: Monami Construction [CRM #100] — footage's existence prevented formal proceedings

evidence.quote: Insurer's legal team formally requested Evercam footage extraction with chain-of-custody documentation for use in a £200k+ property damage subrogation claim — Evercam support assisted with local recording extraction and provided a technical confirmation letter.

workflows.conclusion: A formally preserved and authenticated footage package is delivered to the legal team or adjudicator. Footage either resolves the proceeding or forms the cornerstone of the evidence bundle.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: When a construction dispute escalates to formal legal proceedings, Evercam footage is retrieved, preserved, and packaged as formal evidence. Evercam support assists with high-resolution local recording extraction and chain-of-custody documentation.

workflows.name: Stockpile, Earthworks & Volume Quantity Tracking
workflows.notes: Key distinction from general invoice disputes: earthworks quantities require spatial measurement. Drone surveys are point-in-time snapshots, not continuous.

steps.description: Earthworks/haulage subcontractor submits payment application claiming volume or load count.
Main contractor's QS reviews and identifies discrepancy with site records.
Drone survey commissioned over earthworks area/stockpile.
Drone imagery processed into 3D point cloud and surface model.
Processed data used to calculate volumes and compare against claimed quantities.
Where drone not available, fixed camera recordings reviewed for earthworks activity timeline.
Drone volumetric data and/or camera evidence presented to subcontractor.
Parties negotiate settlement based on objective survey data.
Agreed volumes recorded and payment application adjusted/certified.
Drone survey data and camera records archived as definitive measurement record.

workflows.trigger: Subcontractor/haulier submits payment application claiming earthworks volumes/stockpile quantities the main contractor's QS cannot independently verify.
workflows.activity: Using drone-captured photogrammetric surveys and/or fixed camera recordings to independently measure/estimate earthworks volumes and stockpile quantities.

evidence.quote: The main contractor's QS used drone footage to challenge a haulage subcontractor's claim for earthworks removal — the drone survey of the stockpile at month end showed approximately 30% less material than the claimed volume implied, leading to a £120k reduction in the certified payment.

A cut-and-fill earthworks subcontractor on a highways project disputed the QS's measurement of the completed earthworks. A drone photogrammetric survey was commissioned and the resulting volume calculation, compared against the original ground model, resolved the dispute in favour of the QS's position.

Fixed Evercam cameras overlooking a materials compound were used to cross-reference a stockpile delivery claim — the camera footage showed the number of lorry movements during the claimed delivery period did not match the delivery tickets submitted, providing grounds for a payment reduction.

workflows.conclusion: Quantity dispute resolved — subcontractor's claimed volumes verified and paid, or drone/camera evidence demonstrates discrepancy and payment adjusted.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam drone footage and fixed camera recordings used to visually estimate and verify earthworks volumes, stockpile quantities, and cut-and-fill progress.

workflows.name: Variation & Scope Change Claim Validation
workflows.notes: Sits at the intersection of Subcontractor Invoice Dispute Resolution and Dispute Resolution — Legal Evidence Retrieval.

steps.description: A variation order claim or scope dispute is raised — subcontractor submits a VO claim, main contractor raises a VO to the client, or a scope dispute surfaces during a meeting.
QS or PM reviews the claim and identifies the time period, location, and nature of the alleged change or additional work.
PM or site manager accesses Evercam and navigates to the relevant date/time window and camera(s).
Footage reviewed to determine what work was performed, which trades were present, and whether scope deviates from the original contract.
Where the dispute concerns quantities, Gate Report data cross-referenced to verify truck movements, delivery counts, and timing.
Where the dispute concerns installation completeness, 360° captures from the relevant period reviewed to provide element-level visual confirmation.
Relevant footage clips, 360° frame exports, or Gate Report data extracts compiled as evidence.
Evidence presented to the disputing party — subcontractor, client, or their respective QS teams.
Disputing party reviews visual evidence and either withdraws, adjusts, or maintains their claim.
If claim is maintained despite footage evidence, package escalated to formal dispute resolution — but in the majority of evidenced cases, footage resolves the dispute before this stage.
Variation order settled — approved, adjusted, or closed — and project cost plan updated accordingly.

workflows.trigger: A subcontractor submits a variation order or change claim for additional work — or a scope dispute arises during a meeting when a party alleges work was done (or not done).
workflows.activity: Retrieving and reviewing historical Evercam footage to establish a factual visual record of what work was performed, when, and by whom.

evidence.quote: Main contractor used Evercam cloud recordings to verify the extent of groundworks completed by a subcontractor in a disputed earthworks variation claim — footage confirmed the excavation depth claimed was not reached, reducing the VO value by approximately 30%.
Aidan was able to pull out his phone, open 360 view on the mobile app and show that the works had already been done. This saved time and reduced the need for written documentation.
evidence.source: Westridge Donnybrook [CRM #22] — live in-meeting 360° resolution of a disputed scope completion claim

evidence.quote: QS used Evercam recordings to verify that a subcontractor's claimed additional works (temporary protection installation) were actually within the original contract scope — saving the main contractor from approving an unjustified variation order.

workflows.conclusion: The variation claim is resolved using visual evidence — either validated, reduced, or withdrawn. Formal adjudication avoided.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam cloud recordings, 360° captures, and Gate Report data are used to verify what work was or was not performed — enabling validation or refutation of a variation order claim.

workflows.name: Workers' Compensation & False Injury Claim Defence
workflows.notes: Two sub-variants: (a) genuine workplace injury investigations; (b) suspected fraudulent/exaggerated claims where footage directly disproves the claimant's account.

steps.description: Worker sustains or reports an injury on site, or a third party makes a personal injury or liability allegation against the contractor.
Contractor's safety manager and/or project manager formally notified of the claim.
Internal incident investigation initiated in accordance with the contractor's safety management system.
Safety manager or PM identifies which Evercam camera(s) cover the location of the reported incident and determines the relevant time window.
Evercam cloud recordings accessed and reviewed for the relevant time period. Local recording export requested if incident parameters exceed cloud clip scope.
Footage reviewed frame-by-frame to reconstruct the exact sequence of events — worker location, task, PPE in use, prescribed protocols followed.
Key frames or clips extracted and preserved as evidence. Footage flagged for retention.
Safety manager prepares formal incident investigation report, referencing footage as supporting evidence.
Footage and investigation report provided to the contractor's insurer and, where appropriate, legal counsel.
Insurer reviews footage alongside the claim. If footage shows clear non-compliance or contradicts the claimant's account, claim is denied or renegotiated.
Where the claim involves suspected fraud, footage may be disclosed to the claimant's legal representative under formal legal proceedings.
Claim outcome recorded and incident file closed. Footage retained for the applicable statutory limitation period.

workflows.trigger: A site worker sustains or reports an injury and files a workers' compensation claim — or a third party alleges injury and initiates a personal liability claim.
workflows.activity: Retrieving and reviewing Evercam footage to reconstruct the sequence of events before, during, and after the reported injury.

evidence.quote: Barnhill used video footage from Evercam to investigate a workers' comp claim — saved Barnhill $35k of direct costs. Footage showed the worker had placed a ladder in a puddle without a spotter, a clear safety protocol violation.
A worker was found on the ground. The client has requested assistance in reviewing available camera footage to better understand the timeline of events. Please preserve all available footage.

Contractor used Evercam recordings to refute a claim from a third-party pedestrian who alleged they were struck by a vehicle exiting the site — footage showed the pedestrian had crossed against a traffic signal, redirecting liability entirely.

workflows.conclusion: Footage-based evidence submitted to the insurer and/or legal team. Claim denied, settled at reduced value, or accepted. Footage compressed investigation timeline.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam cloud and local recordings are retrieved after a workplace injury claim is filed, to reconstruct the incident timeline and determine whether the worker followed prescribed safety protocols.

workflows.name: Dig Permit & Underground Utility Clearance Documentation
workflows.notes: The cautionary inverse case (trench drain cut in wrong location when the camera was unplugged) illustrates what this workflow prevents.

steps.description: An excavation scope identified; permit-to-dig raised specifying location, depth, dimensions, and utility clearance requirements.
Utility records obtained from service providers; excavation area marked out on surface.
CAT (Cable Avoidance Tool) and Genny scan conducted over the marked excavation area; result recorded on permit.
Camera footage covering the excavation area confirmed live and recording before the pre-dig inspection begins.
Pre-dig inspection and sign-off conducted at the excavation face — captured on camera with a visible timestamp.
Hand-dig trial holes excavated within the permit zone to physically confirm absence or location of underground services. Camera footage records this step.
Mechanical excavation commences within approved parameters. Camera provides continuous record.
If a utility unexpectedly encountered, work stops immediately. Camera footage from steps 4–7 immediately preserved as evidence that the permit procedure was followed.
On completion, permit closed out and signed off. Camera footage archive linked to the permit record.
Footage retained for the contractual liability period in case of a delayed utility strike claim or regulatory investigation.

workflows.trigger: A ground excavation activity is planned in an area with known or suspected underground utilities. Alternatively, a utility strike has occurred and an investigation requires whether the permit procedure was followed.
workflows.activity: Documenting through camera footage that permit-to-dig process steps — utility mark-out, CAT scan sweep, hand-dig trial holes, and pre-dig sign-off — were completed before any mechanical excavation commenced.

evidence.quote: Timestamped camera evidence used to document that utility clearance checks and permit-to-dig procedures were completed before ground excavation commenced.

Contractor cut trench drain in the wrong location — camera was unplugged at the critical moment, resulting in a $40k error with no footage to establish procedure compliance or responsibility. This directly evidences the cost of the workflow's absence.
evidence.source: CRM #28 — cautionary inverse; illustrates the value of continuous coverage

evidence.quote: The ability to remotely check work zones helped avoid multiple daily trips across the site.
evidence.source: ACCIONA Australia [CRM #11] — pattern of camera coverage for pre-activity compliance documentation on large civil sites

workflows.conclusion: A complete visual record exists confirming that the permit-to-dig procedure was followed.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam camera recordings provide timestamped visual documentation that permit-to-dig procedures were observed before ground excavation commenced.

workflows.name: GDPR / Data Privacy Compliance for Camera Deployment
workflows.notes: Unique workflow — enabling compliance prerequisite for all other camera-based workflows. International variants: US (CCPA, BIPA), Australia (Privacy Act 1988). Product gap: Evercam lacks DPIA template, GDPR checklist, automated retention enforcement.

steps.description: Main contractor identifies legal basis for processing — typically legitimate interests under GDPR Article 6(1)(f).
Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) completed.
Data subject notification signage designed and installed at site entrances and camera locations.
Evercam user accounts provisioned with role-based access controls.
Camera-level access permissions configured in Evercam platform.
Data retention periods configured — automatic deletion/archiving schedules.
Access log and audit trail maintained through Evercam platform.
Procedures established for responding to Subject Access Requests (SARs).
Data breach response procedure documented.
At project close-out, retained footage deleted or transferred to archive with justification documented.

workflows.trigger: New construction project begins with camera deployment decision (GDPR obligation triggered); or DPO/legal team raises compliance query about existing deployment.
workflows.activity: Establishing and documenting full legal/operational compliance framework — lawful basis, data subject notification, access controls, retention periods, subject access request procedures.

evidence.quote: Detailed client query regarding GDPR compliance obligations for camera deployment — covering signage requirements at site entrances and camera locations, access control configuration, data retention periods, and procedures for handling subject access requests.

Under GDPR Article 35, organisations deploying systematic CCTV monitoring in the workplace are required to complete a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) prior to deployment — a non-negotiable legal precondition for compliant camera use on sites in EU/UK jurisdictions.

The UK ICO's CCTV Code of Practice and the Irish DPC's guidance on workplace surveillance both specify that data subjects must be informed of camera monitoring through clear, prominently placed signage identifying the data controller and the purposes of processing.

workflows.conclusion: Camera deployment confirmed as compliant with data protection legislation. Documentation in place sufficient for regulatory audit or data subject complaint.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam platform-level access controls, data retention settings, user permission management, and audit trail capabilities enable the data controller to demonstrate GDPR/data protection compliance.

workflows.name: Noise & Operating Hours Compliance Monitoring
workflows.notes: Product gap: Evercam capability is visual only; no integrated audio/decibel monitoring. Strong for hours compliance but weak for decibel-level noise complaints.

steps.description: Permitted working hours established by the planning consent or noise abatement notice and documented in the site's Environmental Management Plan.
Reactive: a complaint received from a neighbour or council officer. Specific dates and times alleged are recorded.
Proactive: site manager establishes routine of checking recordings at the permitted start and finish times to verify no activity occurred outside the window.
Relevant Evercam recordings accessed for the time period in question — typically 30–60 minutes bracketing the alleged violation or the permitted hours boundary.
Footage reviewed to confirm whether plant, workers, or deliveries were active outside permitted hours.
Recordings are timestamped and relevant clips extracted — showing either the absence (compliance) or presence (breach) of activity.
Reactive: formal written response prepared, citing timestamped footage as evidence. Submitted to the council officer or planning enforcement team.
Proactive: if compliant, monitoring record archived. If breach identified, site manager issues immediate corrective instruction and documents action taken.
Complaint withdrawn or dismissed, compliance confirmed, or internal corrective action closed out.

workflows.trigger: Reactive: a neighbour or local authority makes a formal complaint alleging out-of-hours working. Or proactive: site manager initiates routine daily monitoring to verify compliance.
workflows.activity: Reviewing timestamped camera recordings to establish the precise pattern of site activity relative to the permitted working hours window.

evidence.quote: We can track any work prior to 7:00am. This will help us mitigate any noise complaints that the township may falsely claim.
evidence.source: J.T. Magen / Netflix NJ [Compliance #4] — proactive monitoring variant

evidence.quote: Avoided dispute with council about use of crane after hours.

Project subject to specific planning consent conditions requiring proof of compliance with agreed working hours — establishing this as a distinct, planning-driven trigger rather than a general monitoring activity.
evidence.source: CRM #22 — planning condition driving the workflow

workflows.conclusion: Evidence used to either formally respond to a complaint (closing it without penalty), proactively demonstrate compliance, or identify an internal breach and correct it.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam camera recordings serve as the primary evidence source to prove that construction activity did or did not occur outside permitted working hours.

workflows.name: Noise, Community & Environmental Compliance Monitoring
workflows.notes: Three sub-variants: (i) out-of-hours working complaints (most common); (ii) traffic/vehicle routing complaints; (iii) environmental compliance (contaminated waste).

steps.description: Complaint received from neighbour/resident/local authority, or proactive compliance review triggered by planning condition.
Specific allegation documented — date, time, nature of alleged activity.
PM/site manager accesses Evercam cloud recordings for relevant cameras and time window.
Footage reviewed frame-by-frame across the alleged period.
For vehicle-related complaints, Gate Report ANPR records exported.
Where noise monitoring deployed, noise data aligned with visual record.
Footage clips and Gate Report exports compiled into formal compliance response.
Response submitted to complainant, local authority, or planning department.
If compliant, complaint closed; if breach, corrective action plan drafted and implemented.
All evidence archived in project compliance file.

workflows.trigger: Neighbour/resident group/local authority complaint about noise/out-of-hours working/nuisance; or planning condition requires proactive compliance demonstration.
workflows.activity: Retrieving and reviewing timestamped camera recordings and Gate Report ANPR data to establish factual record of site activity relative to permitted conditions.

evidence.quote: We can track any work prior to 7:00am. This will help us mitigate any noise complaints that the township may falsely claim.
Avoided dispute with council about use of crane after hours.
They check for contaminated muck away being disposed of properly. Check the locations on the camera to make sure they are going to the right places.
evidence.source: GMC Utilities [Compliance #53] — environmental monitoring via Gate Report

workflows.conclusion: Compliance review concludes with footage demonstrating compliance (complaint rebutted) or breach identified (contractor acknowledges, implements corrective action).
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam camera recordings serve as primary evidence for verifying whether construction activity occurred within/outside permitted working hours. Timestamped footage replaces paper-based site diary entries as evidential standard for noise complaints and community disputes.

workflows.name: Regulatory / OSHA / HSE Investigation Support
workflows.notes: Critical distinction from internal workers' compensation investigation: statutory compulsion — contractor cannot selectively withhold adverse footage. Product gap: no in-platform "legal hold" feature preventing accidental deletion.

steps.description: Reportable incident occurs on site.
Contractor complies with immediate statutory notification obligation.
Upon notification receipt, contractor's safety manager/legal counsel instructs Evercam to preserve footage.
Regulatory investigator requests disclosure of all relevant evidence.
Contractor's legal counsel reviews Evercam footage before disclosure.
Relevant footage extracted and compiled into structured evidence package.
Evidence package disclosed to investigator in specified format and timescale.
Regulatory investigator reviews footage alongside other evidence.
Contractor prepares formal written response referencing footage evidence.
Investigation concludes with formal decision and contractor implements any remediation.
All footage, correspondence, and legal advice archived under privilege.

workflows.trigger: Statutory safety regulator formally notifies contractor of investigation following a reportable accident, dangerous occurrence, or specified near-miss.
workflows.activity: Preserving, reviewing, and formally disclosing Evercam footage to the regulatory investigator.

evidence.quote: Regulatory investigation initiated following a reportable workplace incident — Evercam footage retrieved, preserved, and formally disclosed to the statutory investigator as part of the contractor's evidence submission; footage provided the timestamped visual record of the incident sequence and the pre-incident working conditions.

Barnhill used video footage from Evercam to investigate a workers' comp claim — saved Barnhill $35k of direct costs. Footage showed the worker had placed a ladder in a puddle without a spotter, a clear safety protocol violation.
evidence.source: Barnhill Contracting [Insurance #12] — parallel internal and regulatory investigation

evidence.quote: A worker was found on the ground. The client has requested assistance in reviewing available camera footage to better understand the timeline of events. Please preserve all available footage.
evidence.source: JFK Terminal 1B [Compliance #28] — footage preservation and timeline reconstruction for investigation

workflows.conclusion: Regulatory investigation concludes. Evercam footage supports contractor's defence or informs remediation plan.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam cloud and local high-frame-rate recordings retrieved, preserved, and disclosed in response to formal statutory safety regulator investigation requests.

workflows.name: Sustainability & Environmental Impact Reporting

flags.description: Low confidence (5+ records). Most workflow steps are inferred from industry context rather than evidenced by customer records. Current Evercam data contribution is manual (Gate Report spreadsheet exports). Human curator should verify whether any customers are actively using Evercam data in formal sustainability reporting.

workflows.notes: Currently characterised by manual data extraction — Gate Report exports are spreadsheets, not structured CO₂ inputs. Significant product opportunity: Gate Report is the single most commercially important Evercam data source for this workflow.

steps.description: Project sustainability reporting requirements established — identifying the certification framework and the specific indicators to be reported.
Sustainability manager reviews available Evercam data streams to identify which indicators Evercam can contribute to (Gate Report vehicle counts, time-lapse, waste vehicle monitoring, drone imagery).
Gate Report data exported for the reporting period — vehicle entry/exit records formatted for input into CO₂ calculation tool.
Time-lapse footage reviewed or sampled to document site operational patterns and confirm working hours compliance.
Waste vehicle monitoring data compiled to demonstrate compliance with the Site Waste Management Plan.
Drone imagery used to document site boundary, vegetation management, and ecological buffer zones at defined intervals.
All Evercam-sourced data compiled into the sustainability report alongside other data sources and formatted for submission.
Evercam data cited in the evidence appendix with platform-generated timestamps to demonstrate data integrity.
Certification body or client reviews the submission and requests clarification if required.
Certification awarded or ESG report accepted. Data extraction and reporting workflow documented for future reporting cycles.

workflows.trigger: A project team is required to produce a sustainability report or contribute to a CO₂/environmental impact assessment as a contractual obligation, client ESG mandate, or planning condition.
workflows.activity: Extracting and integrating relevant Evercam data streams into the project's sustainability reporting or CO₂ accounting workflow.

evidence.quote: Integrating site camera data with sustainability reporting workflows — confirming customer demand for Evercam data to contribute to CO₂ and environmental impact assessments.
CO₂ reporting integration identified as an emerging customer need across multiple categories — establishing the workflow as a cross-cutting requirement rather than an isolated use case.
Reports on productivity — how many trucks come into the site, any missing dockets. Any invoices too high.
evidence.source: GMC Utilities [Compliance #53] — vehicle movement data captured for billing is structurally identical to transport data required for CO₂ reporting; underlying asset already exists, awaiting sustainability output formatting

workflows.conclusion: Sustainability report submitted with Evercam-sourced data contributing to specific indicators. Documented repeatable process established for future reporting cycles.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam site camera data — including Gate Report vehicle movement records, time-lapse footage, and drone imagery — integrated with the project's sustainability reporting framework.

workflows.name: Client Handover & Completion Celebration Video
workflows.notes: Time-lapse completion videos have moved from premium add-on to baseline expectation. Product gap: no native video editing/compilation tool.

steps.description: At project mobilisation, time-lapse recording configured on primary overview cameras.
As project progresses, milestone events identified and footage bookmarked.
Drone flights commissioned at key project phases.
360° capture walkthroughs conducted at major interior milestones.
At practical completion, PM/marketing team contacts media team to commission video.
Evercam exports full time-lapse archive for the project duration.
Video editor compiles footage into structured narrative (2–5 minutes).
Draft reviewed by PM, marketing team, and client; amendments made.
Final video presented at handover/celebration event.
Contractor publishes video on website, social media, and submits for award programmes.

workflows.trigger: Project approaches practical completion, a major milestone event is planned, or the client formally requests a project video as a contractual/commercial deliverable.
workflows.activity: Compiling project time-lapse archive with milestone recordings, drone footage, and 360° capture into a structured completion video.

evidence.quote: The contractor described producing a completion video for their client's grand opening event — "we gave them the full journey from empty site to finished building in four minutes, set to music, and it was the centrepiece of their opening ceremony." The footage was drawn entirely from Evercam's continuous time-lapse archive.

The client had not formally specified a completion video in the contract, but the contractor produced one as a goodwill gesture at handover — the client subsequently requested the same deliverable on their next two projects with the same contractor, effectively making it a standing requirement.

workflows.conclusion: Completion video formally presented to client at handover/celebration event. Contractor retains copy for marketing portfolio and award submissions.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam time-lapse footage captured continuously throughout the project compiled into a polished completion video documenting the full construction journey from groundbreaking to handover.

workflows.name: Industry Event & Conference Content Production
workflows.notes: Distinct from Social Media Content (Workflow 14): higher production values, expert peer audience, formal submission format. Vivid example: Evercam footage used at Diggers and Dealers Mining Forum (Evolution Mining).

steps.description: Relevant industry event, award programme, or documentary production opportunity identified — by the contractor's marketing/BD team or project director.
Decision made to enter the project for consideration — an award submission, a conference presentation slot, or a documentary interview confirmed.
Marketing or project team reviews available Evercam footage — time-lapse videos, progress recordings, drone clips, 360° walk sequences.
Request made to Evercam (or directly within TLC/TLP) to generate a polished time-lapse covering the relevant project period.
Generated time-lapse reviewed and refined — start/end dates adjusted, playback speed tuned, branding overlays applied.
[Inferred] Footage exported and imported into professional video editing software (e.g., Adobe Premiere) and combined with drone footage, narration, music, and graphics.
Completed video embedded into the conference presentation deck or submitted as part of the award entry package.
For award submissions: entry reviewed by judges, with the time-lapse serving as primary evidence of project execution quality.
For conference presentations: footage presented live to the delegate audience, with the PM or director narrating over the time-lapse.
[Inferred] Post-event, presentation footage and any award recognition repurposed for social media, the company website, and BD materials.

workflows.name: BIM vs. Reality Comparison & Design Verification
workflows.notes: One of Evercam's most technically differentiated workflows — the BIM integration capability distinguishes Evercam from basic CCTV or photo-documentation tools.

BIM overlay applied to the live camera image or 360° photograph, aligning the 3D model to the as-built perspective.

Screenshot or clip of the overlay showing the deviation captured and attached to an RFI or defect notice in the project management system.
RFI assigned to the relevant subcontractor or design team member for resolution.

Milestone sign-off documentation updated to reflect the verified as-built condition.
BIM comparison record retained as part of the as-built documentation package at project completion.

workflows.activity: Comparing as-built site conditions directly against the BIM or design model to verify that structure, MEP installations, finishes, or sequence are correct — identifying deviations before they become costly defects.

workflows.conclusion: Comparison confirms compliance or identifies a deviation that is documented, assigned as an RFI or defect, and corrected before being buried by subsequent work.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam's BIM integration overlays the 3D BIM model directly onto live or recorded camera views of the site, enabling engineers and PMs to compare as-built conditions against the design model in real time without a site visit.

workflows.activity: Conducting systematic pre-construction condition survey — using 360° for interior/adjacent buildings, fixed cameras for external areas/boundaries, drone for aerial overview.

evidence.quote: Before commencing demolition works adjacent to a Victorian terrace, the contractor used Evercam 360° capture to document the existing condition of party walls, cracked brickwork, and existing settlement in neighbouring properties — "without that record, we'd have no defence against any crack that appeared during piling."

The client's legal team required a full pre-construction condition survey as a contract condition. The contractor used 360° capture and fixed cameras to produce a comprehensive baseline record that was formally submitted to the client and archived — referenced eighteen months later when a neighbour claimed that site traffic had damaged their driveway (the pre-construction record showed the damage pre-existed construction).

workflows.conclusion: Baseline condition record complete and archived. Record available for immediate retrieval throughout project and post-completion liability period.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam cameras and 360° capture deployed at project mobilisation to create comprehensive timestamped visual record of site conditions before construction commences.

workflows.name: Remote Site Monitoring & Progress Checking
workflows.notes: This is the highest-frequency day-to-day use of Evercam across all source categories and represents the platform's primary value proposition in daily operations. The Verizon record represents the most commercially significant variant — Evercam enabled a single NJ-based PM to manage midwest US sites remotely, replacing the need for a full-time regional hire.

steps.description: PM, superintendent, or senior manager opens the Evercam platform on desktop or mobile at the start of the day or upon receiving an alert, notification, or query.
Live view accessed across one or more cameras to confirm that site activity has commenced and manpower levels are as expected for the day's planned scope.
Scrub-back / playback used to review overnight or early-morning periods — checking for incidents, unauthorised access, or early-start trades.
PTZ cameras panned or zoomed to specific work zones of interest where critical or schedule-sensitive activity is planned.
If an issue or anomaly is identified, the supervisor either investigates further via footage playback or contacts the site foreman or manager directly.
Snapshots or short clips captured to document current conditions or flag a specific observation for sharing.
Supervisor updates their daily log, morning report, or stakeholder communication based on camera observations — without needing to physically visit the site.
For large sites, the camera check replaces multiple internal site traversals throughout the day, not just external travel.
Dedicated monitors in the site office display continuous live feeds, enabling passive background monitoring alongside active checks.

workflows.trigger: The start of the working day, an incoming report of an incident or concern, or a routine need to verify site conditions — initiated by a PM, superintendent, senior manager, or owner who is not physically present on site.
workflows.activity: Checking live or recently recorded camera footage via the Evercam platform to assess manpower levels, confirm that scheduled activities are underway, identify any overnight or early-morning incidents, and gather enough visual information to direct decisions without a site visit.

evidence.quote: Evercam essentially saved us from having to hire a new Verizon PM for the midwest. With Evercam, I can remote project manage the jobs in the midwest from NJ.
He uses Evercam daily to see the site activity and manpower on site — uses the cameras every morning to check for incidents on site and document progress.

Supervisors used the scrub-back tool to monitor early-morning activity without needing to leave the site office. The ability to remotely check work zones helped avoid multiple daily trips across the site.

workflows.conclusion: The PM, supervisor, or remote stakeholder has a sufficient and accurate picture of site status to direct their day, issue instructions to site staff, respond to an incident, or update stakeholders — without having physically visited the site.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam live camera feeds and recorded playback entirely replace the need for a PM, superintendent, or senior manager to physically travel to site to check on activity, manpower levels, and general site conditions.

workflows.name: Schedule / Milestone Progress Verification
workflows.notes: This workflow sits at the intersection of programme management, commercial management, and claims. The key distinction from Workflow 1 (Remote Monitoring) is intentionality: this workflow begins with a specific question about programme compliance and ends with a documented answer.

steps.description: A programme review trigger occurs — a scheduled review, a delay reported by the site manager, an approaching milestone payment date, or a subcontractor's completion claim.
PM or planning engineer identifies specific activities in the programme that need visual verification and notes the relevant date ranges and site areas.
Evercam recordings or time-lapse accessed for the relevant periods and camera views covering the work areas in question.
Footage reviewed to assess actual progress — what was built, when work started and stopped, worker numbers deployed, plant and materials on site.
Compare/snapshot tool used to generate before-and-after images of key areas at milestone dates, enabling a rapid visual assessment of progress increment.
Time-lapse sequences reviewed at accelerated rate to assess activity patterns — identifying periods of inactivity, slow mobilisation, or weekend working.
Observations documented and compared against the baseline programme. Delays quantified in days.
Where a delay is identified, footage evidence used to notify the relevant subcontractor, build an EOT/prolongation record, or brief senior management.
If subcontractor underperformance is identified, footage triggers a formal written notice of delay or a recovery plan discussion.
Visual record archived as part of contemporaneous project documentation, available for future claims or disputes.

workflows.trigger: A scheduled programme review meeting, a reported or suspected delay to a critical-path activity, a milestone payment point approaching, or a subcontractor's completion claim that needs visual verification against the programme.
workflows.activity: Reviewing Evercam footage, time-lapse, or snapshot comparisons against the planned programme to confirm whether work has progressed at the expected rate and build a contemporaneous visual record to support schedule-related claims.

evidence.quote: They are using time-lapse and recordings to monitor subcontractor progress against the programme and to identify delays for EOT claims.
Camera footage used to compare planned vs. actual progress at milestone dates — screenshot comparison provided visual proof of delay quantum for the client.
Used recordings to verify that the concrete sub was not delivering the agreed number of pours per week — used as basis for formal delay notice.

workflows.conclusion: The programme review is completed with visual evidence either confirming on-schedule progress or identifying and quantifying a delay, incorporated into the programme update or a formal EOT claim package.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam camera footage, time-lapse sequences, and the compare/snapshot tool are used alongside the project programme to visually verify whether work on site is tracking to plan — identifying delays, confirming milestone completions, and generating footage-backed evidence for EOT or prolongation claims.

workflows.name: AI-Powered Safety Intelligence & SIF Detection
workflows.notes: The "aspirational" qualification reflects current deployment state. False positive rates must be managed carefully; excessive spurious alerts create alert fatigue. Commercial implication: safety teams willing to pay premium pricing for demonstrated SIF reduction capability.

steps.description: AI safety analytics module configured for the project — defining detection classes (PPE, zone intrusion, plant-person proximity, fall protection) and cameras.
Detection thresholds and alert rules set — specifying conditions that trigger immediate alert vs. observation, and which personnel receive notifications.
Live camera feeds continuously processed by the AI analytics engine during working hours.
When a trigger condition detected, system generates a real-time alert including a screenshot or clip, camera location, and violation type — dispatched to safety manager.
Safety manager receives the alert and reviews the attached footage clip to assess severity.
If condition confirmed as a genuine violation, safety manager contacts site supervisor or nearest competent person by radio to intervene immediately.
Ground operative locates the worker or activity in question and corrects the unsafe condition.
Incident logged as a near-miss in the safety management system, with the AI detection clip attached.
Safety performance data from the AI system aggregated into weekly/monthly intelligence report identifying systemic risk patterns.
Repeat offenders or persistent high-risk zones escalated to the project safety plan for structural intervention.

workflows.trigger: A safety violation or SIF precursor condition is detected by the AI system on a live camera feed.
workflows.activity: Automated AI analysis of live Evercam camera feeds to detect defined safety risk conditions and dispatch real-time alerts to designated safety personnel.

evidence.quote: AI-automated analysis of site footage to detect serious safety risks in real time — describing an autonomous detection system for SIF precursors rather than a human-reviewed monitoring workflow.
Real-time AI detection of high-risk safety conditions on site — confirming the distinct character of this workflow as an automated intelligence layer over live camera feeds.
The ability to remotely check work zones helped avoid multiple daily trips across the site.
evidence.source: ACCIONA Australia [CRM #11] — foundational remote safety monitoring behaviour that AI detection extends from reactive to proactive

workflows.conclusion: Alert received, condition investigated, ground operative intervenes, near-miss logged. Detection event recorded as a leading indicator.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam's AI-powered video analytics layer autonomously analyses site footage in real time to detect Serious Injury and Fatality (SIF) precursors and dispatches automated alerts to the safety manager.

workflows.name: Crane & High-Risk Lift Monitoring
workflows.notes: Absence of automated exclusion zone alerts limits proactive intervention. PTZ particularly valuable for crane monitoring. Cross-workflow: feeds into Regulatory Investigation (Workflow 27).

steps.description: Lift plan and method statement prepared by appointed person.
Pre-lift toolbox talk conducted with relevant personnel.
Evercam camera positions reviewed to confirm lift zone/exclusion area coverage.
Prior to lift, site manager accesses Evercam live view to confirm exclusion zone is clear.
Lift proceeds under appointed person/crane operator direction with Evercam remote visibility.
Evercam records full lift with timestamps — load attachment, path, placement, release.
For complex/critical lifts, designated team monitors live feed and can issue stop instruction.
Post-lift, footage reviewed to confirm operation proceeded per method statement.
In event of incident/near-miss, footage immediately preserved and incident investigation initiated.
Lift records — method statement, toolbox talk, Evercam footage reference — archived in safety file.

workflows.trigger: Crane mobilised and scheduled lifts programmed; or specific high-risk/complex lift requiring method statement/appointed person — requiring remote visibility and recording capability.
workflows.activity: Using Evercam cameras to monitor crane lift operations in real time, verifying exclusion zone clearance and capturing a continuous timestamped video record.

evidence.quote: Evercam cameras used to monitor crane lift operations in real time, providing site management with remote visibility of lift zone activity and capturing a continuous timestamped record of all crane movements — footage subsequently used to review post-lift compliance with the method statement and to demonstrate safe working practices to the client.
Avoided dispute with council about use of crane after hours.
evidence.source: Bennetts Construction [Compliance #85] — crane footage serving both safety and community compliance functions

evidence.quote: Under HSE Guidance L113 (Safe Use of Lifting Equipment), all lifting operations must be properly planned, appropriately supervised, and carried out in a safe manner — the Evercam monitoring record provides contemporaneous evidence that supervision was in place for the duration of the operation.

workflows.conclusion: Lift operation completed safely with full video record retained. Footage immediately available for investigation in event of incident/near-miss.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam fixed/PTZ cameras positioned to provide real-time visibility of crane operations and high-risk lift zones, allowing remote monitoring of exclusion zone clearance and lift compliance.

workflows.name: Fire Investigation & Hot Work Safety Monitoring
workflows.notes: Key distinctive: time-criticality of footage preservation — fires can destroy on-site infrastructure, making cloud-hosted recordings the sole surviving evidence.

steps.description: Fire/smoke event detected; fire extinguished and site made safe.
Incident reported to safety manager; internal investigation initiated.
Safety manager/site manager immediately accesses Evercam and preserves footage.
Footage reviewed to identify fire origin location and ignition time.
Working backwards, footage reviewed to identify personnel/operations at fire origin in hours preceding ignition.
Relevant hot work permit retrieved and cross-referenced against footage.
Footage reviewed for post-ignition period — spread rate, evacuation, personnel actions.
Footage-based incident timeline prepared.
Timeline and clips provided to insurer's loss adjuster, legal counsel, regulatory investigator.
If subcontractor non-compliance demonstrated, formal cost recovery claim initiated.
Investigation findings used to update hot work permit procedure and training.

workflows.trigger: Fire, smoke event, or hot work near-miss occurs on site; or post-incident fire safety investigation initiated.
workflows.activity: Retrieving and analysing Evercam footage to reconstruct sequence of events — establishing when fire started, where it originated, who was working, and whether hot work permit was complied with.

evidence.quote: Evercam footage retrieved following a site fire to reconstruct the sequence of events — footage identified the area of origin, the time of ignition, and the hot work activities occurring in the vicinity in the hours preceding the fire, providing critical input to both the internal investigation and the insurer's loss adjustment process.

Hot work incident investigated using Evercam recordings — footage reviewed to verify whether the prescribed hot work permit conditions (fire watch, combustible material clearance, permit validity) were followed by the subcontractor conducting the work, enabling the main contractor to assess liability and respond to the insurer's investigation.
The internal CCTV system inside the building was cut during the burglary, leaving Evercam as the only available visual record.
evidence.source: M Property, Footscray [Insurance #1] — directly analogous to fire scenarios where on-site infrastructure is destroyed by the incident

workflows.conclusion: Footage-based investigation report identifies ignition source, sequence of events, and compliance status. Responsibility attributed. Insurance claim lodged.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam cloud and local high-frame-rate recordings retrieved following a fire/hot work incident to establish sequence of events, identify ignition source/location, and determine whether hot work permit procedures were followed.

workflows.name: High-Risk Zone & Restricted Area Monitoring
workflows.notes: Product opportunity: automated breach detection replacing human monitoring. Critical constraint: camera coverage must be pre-validated before activity begins.

steps.description: Pre-activity safety planning identifies zones requiring restricted access.
RAMS completed specifying monitoring requirement for the restricted zone.
Camera positions reviewed to confirm restricted zone coverage.
PTZ camera pre-programmed or manually positioned to cover exclusion zone.
Site safety manager/designated monitor opens Evercam live view.
Live monitoring conducted for duration of high-risk activity.
If unauthorised person enters zone, work halted and individual directed out.
On completion of high-risk activity, zone stood down.
Evercam recordings retained as safety compliance record.
In case of incident, footage immediately preserved and provided to investigating authority.

workflows.trigger: High-risk activity planned/ongoing — crane operations with exclusion zones, deep excavation with collapse risk, proximity to live buried services, or work near energised electrical infrastructure.
workflows.activity: Maintaining continuous or regularly checked visual surveillance of restricted zones to detect unauthorised access, unsafe proximity, or exclusion boundary breach.

evidence.quote: Monitoring of crane exclusion zones and areas where only authorised personnel should be present — continuous surveillance replacing the need for a physical watcher during lift operations.
Pre-activity safety planning integration with camera monitoring of excavation edges and live service corridors — establishing the zone coverage requirement before work commences.
The ability to remotely check work zones helped avoid multiple daily trips across the site.
evidence.source: ACCIONA Australia [CRM #11] — corroborating the remote zone monitoring practice on large civil sites

workflows.conclusion: High-risk activity completed without safety incident. Any exclusion zone breach detected and acted on in real-time. Footage retained as compliance record.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam fixed and PTZ cameras positioned to provide continuous surveillance of designated high-risk zones, replacing the need for a dedicated human watcher/spotter.

workflows.name: Proactive Safety & PPE Compliance Monitoring
workflows.notes: Structurally distinct from Safety Incident Investigation (Workflow 4): this workflow is prospective and preventive (observing live to prevent an event) whereas Workflow 4 is retrospective (reviewing footage after an event).

steps.description: A safety monitoring check is triggered — either scheduled (start of shift, pre-lift check) or ad hoc (receipt of a concern, start of a high-risk activity).
Safety manager or site supervisor opens Evercam live view on desktop or mobile and navigates to the camera(s) covering the relevant work zones.
PTZ cameras directed toward active work areas — elevated platforms, scaffold faces, excavations, crane operation zones.
Live footage observed for PPE compliance (hard hats, hi-vis, harnesses, safety footwear) and behavioural compliance (barriers, exclusion zones, permit conditions).
If non-compliance identified, supervisor contacts the relevant site foreman via radio, phone, or messaging system to issue a correction immediately.
If non-compliance is persistent or involves a specific subcontractor, the footage window is recorded and used as the basis for a formal written safety notice.
The observation — whether compliant or non-compliant — is logged in the site safety record for the period.
For subcontractor-specific patterns of non-compliance, the footage record is used in subcontractor performance reviews or commercial deduction processes.
Where camera coverage is insufficient, the supervisor supplements remote observation with a targeted physical visit to the specific zone of concern.

workflows.trigger: Start of a working period, commencement of a high-risk activity, receipt of a safety concern, or a routine safety walk being impractical due to site size or access constraints.
workflows.activity: Using Evercam live view to remotely observe whether workers are wearing required PPE, following prescribed safe behaviours, and adhering to site safety rules.

evidence.quote: The safety manager checks the live feed every morning before going to site — if he can see workers active without hi-vis or helmets from the camera, he calls the foreman before he even gets out of the car.

We used the camera to monitor the subcontractor's scaffold erection — we could see from the office whether they were clipping on at height. Previously we'd have had to station someone at the base of the scaffold all day.

Contractor cut the trench drain in the wrong location — the camera had been unplugged at the critical moment and there was no footage. It ended up costing $40k that could have been caught much earlier.
evidence.source: CRM #28 — illustrating the financial cost of a monitoring gap

workflows.conclusion: Non-compliant behaviour identified and corrected through immediate intervention or formal safety notice. The supervisor has discharged their supervisory obligation for the period without requiring a physical walk.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam live camera feeds enable safety managers and supervisors to observe worker behaviour, PPE compliance, and adherence to safe systems of work in real time without physically walking to each work zone.

workflows.name: Safety Incident Investigation & Post-Incident Review
workflows.notes: The footage preservation step is critical and time-sensitive. Evercam support's proactive response in the JFK Terminal 1B case illustrates best practice, but this should be a standard protocol triggered automatically on receipt of an injury report.

steps.description: A safety incident is reported — injury, near-miss, structural failure, or environmental event. Safety manager or PM is notified immediately.
Safety manager or PM issues an immediate instruction to preserve all relevant footage — contacting Evercam support if necessary to ensure cloud clips are not overwritten.
Relevant camera(s) and approximate time window are identified — typically working backward from the time the incident was reported or discovered.
Footage reviewed to reconstruct the timeline: pre-incident conditions, the incident event itself, and immediate aftermath.
Specific observations documented — worker behaviour, PPE compliance, equipment state, sequence of actions, presence of supervisors.
Relevant clips extracted and preserved. Local HFR recordings requested from Evercam if the cloud clip resolution or frame rate is insufficient.
Safety manager prepares the formal incident investigation report, citing the footage as supporting evidence and referencing specific timestamps.
Where a workers' compensation or liability claim is involved, footage and report submitted to the insurer and/or legal counsel.
Where a regulatory notification is required (RIDDOR, OSHA, WorkSafe), investigation report supported by footage submitted to the relevant authority.
Incident record, including footage clips, retained in the project archive. Corrective actions documented and tracked.

workflows.trigger: A reportable or non-reportable safety incident occurs on site — a worker injury, near-miss, structural failure, equipment damage, or environmental incident.
workflows.activity: Retrieving, reviewing, and preserving Evercam footage of the incident and the period leading up to it — to reconstruct what happened, identify contributing factors, and produce an evidence base for the formal investigation.

evidence.quote: Barnhill used video footage from Evercam to investigate a workers' comp claim — saved Barnhill $35k of direct costs. Footage showed the worker had set a ladder in a puddle without a spotter, a clear safety protocol violation.
A worker was found on the ground. The client has requested assistance in reviewing available camera footage to better understand the timeline of events. Please preserve all available footage.
Client requested a video to investigate the rebar wall that had buckled/twisted — the video was to give more info to the engineer to help determine the root cause.

workflows.conclusion: A footage-based investigation record is produced and preserved. Submitted to the insurer, regulator, and/or legal counsel. Corrective actions identified and assigned.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam cloud recordings and local high-frame-rate recordings are retrieved after a safety event to reconstruct the sequence of events, identify contributing factors, and provide a timestamped visual record for the formal incident investigation.

workflows.name: Safety Training & Lessons Learned Using Site Footage
workflows.notes: Authentic site-specific footage more impactful than generic training. Cross-workflow links to incident investigation workflows.

steps.description: Safety incident, near-miss, or unsafe act recorded on site.
Safety manager/PM notified and formal incident review initiated.
Evercam recordings reviewed for relevant time window and camera angle.
Footage assessed for clarity, relevance, and sensitivity (personally identifiable information considerations).
Appropriate footage segment selected and exported as a training clip.
Training content developed around the footage — context, root cause analysis, correct procedure.
Toolbox talk or induction session delivered using the footage as the centrepiece.
Attendance recorded and lesson-learned formally documented in the safety management system.
Where footage demonstrates a systemic issue, content shared across business portfolio.

workflows.trigger: Recordable incident, near-miss, or observed unsafe behaviour occurs on site; or periodic safety review cycle creates need for new relevant training content.
workflows.activity: Retrieving and editing Evercam footage of real site events to create training materials demonstrating consequences of unsafe practices.

evidence.quote: Footage of a real near-miss on a live project was used in a subsequent toolbox talk — the site manager described the footage as "far more effective than any training video we've used" because it showed their own site and their own conditions.

Safety manager retrieved a recording of a worker operating plant without a spotter and used it as the basis for a site-wide safety briefing, with the clip played at the start of a weekly safety stand-down.

Following a recordable incident, the contractor's HSE director requested footage be exported and packaged as a lessons-learned case study for distribution to all projects across the business — combining the investigation record with a training narrative.

workflows.conclusion: Footage-based training content delivered. Attendance logged. Lesson-learned formally recorded and shared across business if appropriate.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam cloud recordings and exported video clips of real site incidents, near-misses, and unsafe behaviours used as training material for toolbox talks, induction sessions, and post-incident debriefs.

workflows.name: Vehicle & Plant Safety Incident Investigation

Footage cross-referenced with site traffic management plan.
Incident reconstruction documented in written investigation report.
Footage clips and Gate Report records compiled into evidence package.
If another party at fault, formal liability challenge made to their insurer.
Traffic management plan reviewed and amendments implemented.
Investigation record archived in project safety file.

workflows.trigger: Vehicle/plant incident occurs at site/gate — collision, near-miss with pedestrian, plant in restricted zone, or traffic management violation reported.
workflows.activity: Retrieving, reviewing, and analysing Evercam footage and Gate Report data to reconstruct the incident.

evidence.quote: Vehicle incident at site gate investigated using Evercam camera footage — footage provided a clear timestamped record of the vehicle movements, speeds, and gate configuration at the time of the collision, enabling the contractor to establish the sequence of events and defend against the third party's insurance claim.

Gate camera footage used to investigate a vehicle crash at the site entrance — ANPR data identified the vehicle registration and arrival time, while camera footage reconstructed the incident sequence, providing the contractor with an evidence package for the insurer and police investigation.

Plant machine operating outside its designated zone was captured on Evercam footage — footage reviewed following a near-miss report confirmed the plant operator's non-compliance with the traffic management plan, enabling the contractor to issue a formal non-conformance notice and remove the operator from site pending retraining.

workflows.conclusion: Footage-based incident investigation produces factual timeline. Report submitted to insurer/legal counsel/regulatory authority. Traffic management amendments implemented.

workflows.name: Access Control & User Permission Management
workflows.notes: Platform governance workflow enabling all other Evercam-dependent workflows. Prerequisite for GDPR/data privacy compliance (Workflow 24).

steps.description: New project created on Evercam platform; primary account administrator designated.
Core project team members invited and assigned Admin/Manager roles.
Client representatives invited and assigned appropriate read-level access.
Subcontractor PMs added with project-specific/camera-specific restrictions.
External parties (insurers, H&S consultants) granted time-limited or project-specific access.
Access permissions periodically reviewed to confirm appropriateness.
As project progresses, access adjusted based on evolving team composition.
At practical completion, access for temporary stakeholders removed.
Post-completion, limited long-term access retained for defect investigation period.
Access configuration documented for audit and GDPR compliance.

workflows.trigger: New project set up on Evercam; new stakeholder requires camera access; existing user's role changes; project reaches practical completion; or GDPR/data-privacy review requires access restriction.
workflows.activity: Configuring and maintaining user access permissions — adding/removing users, assigning roles, applying camera-level restrictions, setting access expiry.

evidence.quote: Recurring administrative workflow of managing who has access to which camera feeds across projects — confirming this is a distinct, actively managed workflow rather than a one-time setup.
Role-based access configuration where only Read+Share users can view full video — illustrating the operational specificity of permission management decisions that must be actively maintained.

Gate Report data ring-fenced from client-level users (OPW) — demonstrating that access management has direct commercial and GDPR implications that must be actively managed throughout the project lifecycle.
