workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam platform user management — role-based access levels, project/camera-level permission granularity, ability to add/remove external users — supports the administrative workflow of controlling who sees which feeds, for how long, with what capability.

workflows.name: After-Hours Security Monitoring & Intruder Detection
workflows.notes: Evercam footage alone is frequently insufficient to directly identify suspects — but the precise timestamp is consistently the critical data point that enables police to achieve identification by cross-referencing with public CCTV or traffic camera networks.

steps.description: After-hours incident trigger occurs — a break-in discovered on arrival, a motion alert fires, a security company logs an alarm activation, or PM notices suspicious activity.
Site manager or PM accesses Evercam remotely and navigates to the relevant camera views for the period of suspected activity.
Cloud recordings reviewed to identify nature of incident: entry point, time of first appearance, number of individuals, vehicle(s), route through site, time of departure.
Identifying details noted: vehicle type, colour, partial/full plate, distinctive features of individuals, direction of approach and departure.
If cloud recording resolution is insufficient, a local HFR recording export requested from Evercam support for the relevant time window.
Relevant footage clips exported from the Evercam platform and shared with site security and/or police.
Police provided with precise timestamps of the incident — the primary data point enabling cross-reference with adjacent public CCTV, ANPR, or traffic cameras.
Insurance notification raised if incident involved property damage, theft, or entry to secure areas — footage provided alongside a damage/loss assessment.
Footage retained as a formal record of the incident in the project archive.
Protective responses implemented before the next working day — changed access codes, additional barriers, reinforced perimeter — based on entry method identified from footage.

workflows.trigger: An after-hours breach or suspicious event is identified — found by site staff on arrival, flagged during proactive overnight monitoring, triggered by a third-party security service, or surfaced by a motion detection alert.
workflows.activity: Reviewing Evercam footage from the relevant after-hours time window to establish what occurred, who was involved, when, and what was damaged or removed.

evidence.quote: The timestamps were the key — even though we couldn't read the plate clearly, the police used the exact time from Evercam to pull the vehicle from the council CCTV on the road outside. They had a suspect within 48 hours.
We check the Evercam every morning before we go to site — not just for progress but to see if anything happened overnight. It's become part of the routine.

The intruders smashed the on-site camera on the way out — but because Evercam is cloud-based, the footage was already uploaded and safe. We had a clear recording of them entering even though the camera was destroyed.

workflows.conclusion: A footage clip with timestamps is exported and handed to the police. An insurance notification is raised if property was damaged. Protective measures implemented.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam live view and cloud/local recordings enable PMs, site managers, and security officers to remotely detect, review, and respond to after-hours activity including trespass, break-ins, and unauthorised vehicle access.

workflows.name: Gate Access Control & Vehicle Movement Monitoring
workflows.notes: Gate Report is Evercam's most distinct product in this workflow — it is a structured data system built on ANPR, not simply camera footage.

steps.description: Gate Report cameras installed at site entrance(s) and exit(s), positioned to capture vehicle number plates clearly in both entry and exit directions.
ANPR system configured in Evercam — vehicle categories, vendor tags, and gate designations set up. Known vehicles pre-registered to vendor accounts for automated classification.
Gate Report begins automatically logging all vehicle movements — plate number, timestamp, direction (in/out), vendor tag, and vehicle type.
Site manager or QS reviews Gate Report data daily or weekly — accessing filtered dashboard or exported report to check delivery counts and identify missing dockets.
Where a specific delivery is in question, the relevant entry/exit record located in Gate Report and cross-referenced against the paper or digital delivery docket.
Where a discrepancy is found (e.g., invoice claims 12 deliveries; Gate Report records 9), the data extracted and presented to the supplier as evidence.
Camera recordings at the gate reviewed to provide visual confirmation of vehicle movements, load status, or direction of travel where ANPR data alone is insufficient.
For traffic management compliance, gate recordings reviewed periodically or upon complaint to verify that vehicles are using prescribed routes.
Gate Report data exported (CSV or PDF) for inclusion in monthly progress reports, compliance submissions, or dispute resolution packages.
At project completion, the full Gate Report log serves as an auditable record of all site vehicle movements across the project lifecycle.

workflows.trigger: A construction site gate opens for the working day, or a project commences operations requiring structured tracking of vehicle movements as a contractual, operational, or compliance requirement.
workflows.activity: Automatically recording all vehicle entry and exit events at site gates using ANPR, generating structured gate reports that can be filtered, exported, and cross-referenced.

evidence.quote: The main value of Gate Report has been being able to verify that vehicles are not turning left out of site — a specific term the project agreed on.
evidence.source: Skanska USA [Compliance #46] — contractual traffic management compliance

evidence.quote: Reports on productivity — how many trucks come into the site, any missing dockets. Any invoices too high.
evidence.source: GMC Utilities [Compliance #53] — Gate Report as daily operational management tool

evidence.quote: We manage to save €100k in contractor over-charges.
evidence.source: Glenveagh [Compliance #56] — machine hire verification via Gate Report

workflows.conclusion: A verified, timestamped, exportable log of all vehicle movements exists for the site — enabling delivery reconciliation, invoice validation, compliance reporting, and dispute resolution.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam's Gate Report product (ANPR) is the primary tool for this workflow. It automatically captures, logs, and reports all vehicle entry and exit events at site gates, replacing manual gate logs, sign-in sheets, and paper dockets.

workflows.name: Material & Equipment Theft Investigation
workflows.notes: Distinct from After-Hours Security Monitoring (Workflow 9) by its specific focus on theft of materials/plant and the downstream insurance claim process.

steps.description: Theft discovered on site — by site staff on morning or post-weekend arrival, during a security check, or via a remote Evercam monitoring check.
Site manager or PM immediately accesses Evercam — typically the first port of call before police are called, as footage will determine the scope of the police report.
Time-lapse footage reviewed first at accelerated rate to rapidly narrow the time window of the theft — identifying when items were last visible versus first absent.
Identified time window reviewed at full recording speed, focusing on gate/perimeter cameras and cameras covering the areas where items were stored.
Identifying details extracted: vehicle type/make/colour/plate; number of individuals; clothing; entry and exit points; precise time sequence of the theft.
If cloud recording resolution is insufficient for plate reading or individual identification, a local HFR recording export requested from Evercam support.
Evidence package compiled — exported clips, timestamped screenshots, written summary of observations — organised for sharing.
Police contacted and a formal crime report filed. Evidence package provided to the investigating officer.
Insurance company notified and a formal claim initiated — footage package alongside loss inventory forms the core of the insurance submission.
Police use footage evidence to cross-reference with public CCTV, road ANPR, or traffic cameras — in cases where plates are identifiable, this frequently leads to suspect identification.
Investigation outcome documented in the project security record. Corrective measures implemented.

workflows.trigger: Site personnel arrive to discover that materials, equipment, tools, plant, copper wiring, or other valuable assets have been stolen — typically overnight, over a weekend, or during a bank holiday.
workflows.activity: Retrieving and reviewing Evercam footage — using time-lapse to rapidly narrow the theft window, then full recordings for detailed review — to identify what was taken, when, by whom, and by what means.

evidence.quote: $500,000 worth of stolen materials — footage will be critical for both the investigation and insurance claims. The internal CCTV system inside the building was cut during the burglary, leaving Evercam as the only available visual record.
It helped us identify the vehicle, which was within a mile of the site. And we were able to hold the intruder accountable.
The HFR video we provided clearly shows the intruders.
evidence.source: Sisk Astellas, Tralee [Insurance #13] — footage produced after on-site camera was deliberately smashed

workflows.conclusion: A structured footage evidence package is submitted to the police and insurance company. Police investigation proceeds using footage as primary evidence, sometimes leading to recovery of stolen goods.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam recordings — particularly local high-frame-rate recordings — serve as the primary and often sole visual evidence source for documenting construction site theft events.

workflows.name: Perimeter & Boundary Security Monitoring (Ongoing)
workflows.notes: Passive continuous workflow (differs from After-Hours Security which is reactive). Product gap: automated breach alerting with AI-driven motion classification needed.

steps.description: Site security plan specifies perimeter monitoring requirement.
Evercam cameras installed on hoardings/fencing/structures for overlapping boundary coverage.
Evercam platform configured — cloud recording, motion detection alerts, access permissions assigned.
During working hours, perimeter feeds available for passive monitoring.
After working hours, motion-triggered alerts notify designated personnel.
Daily/weekly perimeter recording review conducted to confirm hoarding integrity.
Any perimeter incident documented — clips exported and filed.
Periodic perimeter audits supported by camera evidence.
At practical completion, cameras recovered and archive retained per retention policy.

workflows.trigger: Site mobilisation and establishment of site compound/perimeter hoarding — at which point planning conditions/site security plan/contractor procedures require perimeter monitoring.
workflows.activity: Continuous passive monitoring of site boundary — recording all perimeter movement, detecting/logging breach attempts, verifying hoarding integrity.

evidence.quote: The site had a specific planning condition requiring continuous perimeter CCTV coverage throughout the construction period. Evercam cameras on the hoarding were the primary compliance mechanism, with the PM able to demonstrate to the planning authority that coverage was maintained through the cloud recording archive.

CDM Regulations (UK) and equivalent frameworks in other jurisdictions require that construction site boundaries are secured and monitored — creating a baseline legal obligation that drives perimeter monitoring as a standard workflow on every project above a minimum size threshold.

Insurance requirements for contractors' all-risk (CAR) and public liability policies typically mandate perimeter security measures. Evercam's cloud-archived perimeter monitoring provides documentary evidence of compliance that can support insurance renewals and claims.
evidence.source: Industry standard — CAR/public liability insurance requirements

workflows.conclusion: Site reaches practical completion and demobilisation. Perimeter cameras recovered. Full archive retained per post-project period. Monitoring obligation formally discharged.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam cameras on site hoardings, perimeter fencing, and boundary structures provide continuous passive monitoring — replacing traditional manned guarding or standalone CCTV.

workflows.name: Drone / Media Platform Migration & Consolidation
workflows.notes: Primarily a commercial and account management opportunity rather than a daily operational workflow. Product gap: Evercam does not offer native photogrammetry processing — customers may still need Pix4D/DroneDeploy for processing.

steps.description: Existing media ecosystem audited — identifying all platforms in use, data types hosted on each, and users who depend on them.
Business case for consolidation assessed — comparing combined subscription cost of existing platforms against Evercam cost.
Evercam account configured to receive drone and media uploads — storage, project structure, and user permissions set up.
Historical drone survey outputs exported from legacy platform in standard formats and imported into Evercam.
Aerial photography and video libraries transferred — either via direct upload or by connecting cloud storage.
Active drone programme workflows reconfigured — drone operator set up to deliver future outputs directly to Evercam.
All project team members and external stakeholders added to the consolidated Evercam environment.
Legacy platform subscriptions cancelled or downgraded once migration confirmed complete.
Evercam used as the single point of access for all future site visual data.

workflows.trigger: A construction team using one or more third-party platforms identifies data fragmentation, rising subscription costs, or a mandate to consolidate all project documentation into a single environment.
workflows.activity: Migrating drone survey outputs, aerial photography, and other site media from third-party platforms into the Evercam platform — and decommissioning or reducing reliance on legacy platform(s).

evidence.quote: Customer migrating drone and site media from third-party platforms (Pix4D, DroneDeploy, etc.) into Evercam — confirming the consolidation trigger and the platform migration steps as an evidenced workflow pattern.
Evercam essentially saved us from having to hire a new Verizon PM for the midwest. With Evercam, I can remote project manage the jobs in the midwest from NJ.
evidence.source: Verizon [CRM #27] — illustrating the high value of centralised single-platform access to all site visual data, which is the ultimate value proposition of media consolidation

evidence.quote: Echelon DUB-10 using gate cameras and site cameras together within a unified Evercam environment — demonstrating the platform's capacity to serve as a multi-data-type site intelligence hub, the destination state for a successful media migration.

workflows.conclusion: All active drone survey data and site media accessible within Evercam. Redundant platform subscriptions cancelled or consolidated.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam acts as the consolidated platform into which drone survey data and site media previously hosted on third-party platforms (Pix4D, DroneDeploy, Propeller) is migrated and centralised.

workflows.name: Drone-Based Site Survey & Aerial Progress Capture
workflows.notes: Distinct modality from fixed cameras — provides coverage, measurement, and perspective unavailable from ground level. Particularly valuable on large civil/infrastructure projects. Periodic rather than continuous.

steps.description: Drone survey scheduled — recurring at set interval or triggered by milestone.
Pre-flight planning completed — airspace clearance, flight path, weather conditions, ground control points.
Drone operator conducts aerial survey capturing nadir and oblique imagery.
Raw imagery processed using photogrammetry software to produce orthomosaic maps, point clouds, or 3D models.
Processed outputs uploaded to Evercam platform.
Project team accesses aerial imagery via Evercam interface for progress review.
Volumetric calculations performed on point cloud for cut/fill/stockpile quantity verification.
Aerial video extracted and compiled into progress highlight reel.
Aerial imagery incorporated into monthly progress report.
All drone outputs archived in project Evercam record for the full project lifecycle.

workflows.trigger: Scheduled survey interval arrives (weekly, fortnightly, monthly), major construction milestone reached, or specific quantity measurement/logistics review required.
workflows.activity: Conducting aerial drone survey, processing imagery into orthomosaic maps/point clouds, hosting output on Evercam platform for progress tracking and verification.

evidence.quote: Drone survey used to capture aerial progress imagery at key construction milestones, with footage compiled for client reporting and stakeholder presentations — providing a whole-site view unavailable from fixed cameras.

Aerial progress capture integrated into weekly stakeholder reporting cycle, with drone output used alongside fixed camera time-lapse and compare-tool images to provide a comprehensive visual progress narrative.

Drone-based quantity measurement used on an earthworks package to verify cut-and-fill volumes and reconcile surveyor's quantities against subcontractor claims — providing an independent aerial measurement record.

workflows.conclusion: Processed aerial imagery/video delivered to project team via Evercam platform; progress compared against programme; quantities verified; visual record archived.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam's drone capture service provides scheduled or triggered aerial site surveys that feed directly into progress reporting and milestone verification workflows, with capability for quantity measurement, cut-and-fill analysis, and logistics overview.

workflows.name: VR / Immersive Site Review

flags.description: Evercam role is currently "none" — VR integration is aspirational with no current product capability. Only 2 evidence records. This entry is retained to track the product opportunity but should be reviewed if/when VR capability is added to the roadmap.

workflows.notes: Documented at prototype/aspirational stage. The distinction from standard 360° Interior Progress Tracking (Workflow 19) is the delivery medium: Workflow 19 uses flat-screen 360 navigation while this uses fully immersive spatial presence via headset.

steps.description: A significant project milestone is identified where a physical site visit is not feasible for a key remote stakeholder.
Site team conducts a 360° capture walkthrough of the relevant areas using Evercam's 360° capture product.
[Aspirational] 360° footage imported into a VR rendering environment (WebXR, Unity, or a construction VR tool such as IrisVR or Fuzor).
[Aspirational] VR environment configured — navigation paths set, key areas annotated with issue markers or milestone labels.
Remote stakeholder accesses the VR environment via headset or high-fidelity browser-based 3D viewer.
[Aspirational] Stakeholder navigates through the site virtually — examining structural elements, spatial layouts, fitout progress, and construction quality.
Stakeholder raises observations, marks up issues, or approves areas — annotations logged and exported as a review record.
Review session concludes; report or issue log generated from VR annotations and shared with on-site team for action.
Physical site visit eliminated or scoped down to address only the specific items raised during the VR review.

workflows.trigger: A senior stakeholder who is geographically remote needs to conduct a meaningful site review that goes beyond flat camera footage at a significant milestone where spatial understanding of the site is important.
workflows.activity: Loading a 360° or multi-camera site capture into a VR headset or immersive browser environment and conducting a simulated walkthrough of the site.

evidence.quote: VR integration aspiration documented — the use of Evercam footage within a VR environment for immersive remote site review — confirming this as a tracked product opportunity with at least one customer-facing conversation evidenced.
Evercam's existing 360° capture capability provides the foundational data layer for this workflow; the gap is solely in immersive rendering and delivery, not in data capture.

Industry adoption of VR for design coordination and client review is growing in sectors including healthcare, aviation, and high-value commercial fitout — particularly where restricted access (live environments, operational facilities) makes physical walkthroughs impractical or expensive.
evidence.source: Industry standard — VR adoption in construction

workflows.conclusion: The remote stakeholder completes the immersive site review, raises concerns for follow-up, and eliminates the need for a physical site visit.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Currently, Evercam has no native VR integration or immersive playback capability. The workflow represents a product opportunity: integrating Evercam's 360° capture footage into VR headset environments for immersive remote site review.

workflows.name: Weighbridge & Tipping Truck Workflow Monitoring

flags.description: Evercam role is currently "none" — weighbridge integration is aspirational with no current product capability. Only 2 evidence records. Entry retained to track the product development opportunity.

workflows.notes: Missing technical component: data integration layer between Gate Report ANPR and weighbridge management software. Gate Report already captures the plate/timestamp data needed; the gap is automated weighbridge data ingestion.

steps.description: Bulk earthworks or demolition subcontract awarded on a per-load or per-tonne payment basis.
[Aspirational] Evercam's Gate Report configured to capture all truck plate numbers and timestamps at the site gate.
[Aspirational] Weighbridge system records gross, tare, and net weight for each truck on each trip.
[Aspirational] Gate Report vehicle movement data exported and cross-referenced against the weighbridge weigh ticket log — matching plate numbers and timestamps.
Discrepancies identified: trucks in Gate Report without a corresponding weigh ticket, anomalously low net weights, or ticket sequences that do not match observed trip counts.
Camera footage at the tipping or loading area reviewed for flagged truck events to visually confirm whether a full tipping event occurred.
Reconciliation report produced — confirmed loads, flagged discrepancies, adjusted tonnage total — presented to the subcontractor with supporting evidence.
Subcontractor's payment application approved at the reconciled tonnage figure; overpayment recovered or deducted from the next application.

workflows.trigger: A bulk earthworks or demolition project is underway where a subcontractor is being paid on a per-load or per-tonne basis and the main contractor needs to verify claimed loads.
workflows.activity: Cross-referencing camera-recorded truck arrival and departure events with weighbridge system records to verify that every claimed load is supported by a corresponding truck movement and valid weigh ticket.

evidence.quote: Weighbridge integration aspiration documented — a desired workflow in which Evercam cameras and weighbridge systems are integrated to verify truck loads — confirming this as a tracked feature development opportunity with a clear commercial use case in bulk earthworks projects.

Evercam's Gate Report ANPR capability already provides the vehicle identification and timestamp layer that forms the basis of this workflow; the gap is the weighbridge data integration, not the camera infrastructure.
evidence.source: Cross-reference — Workflow 13: Gate Access Control & Vehicle Movement Monitoring

evidence.quote: Per-tonne and per-load payment structures are standard on civil earthworks and demolition subcontracts; over-claiming on truck loads is a well-documented industry problem that automated camera-weighbridge reconciliation would directly address.
evidence.source: Industry standard — civil earthworks payment structures

workflows.conclusion: A reconciled load count and tonnage record produced, confirming or identifying a discrepancy. Used to approve, adjust, or dispute the subcontractor's payment application.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Currently, Evercam does not have a native integration with weighbridge systems. The workflow represents a product development opportunity: integrating Evercam's Gate Report ANPR with weighbridge data to automatically cross-reference truck identity, load weight, and tipping event against claimed tonnage.

workflows.name: Internal Staff Visibility & Intranet / Video Wall Integration
workflows.notes: Video wall use case powerful for business development — demonstrates capability to visiting clients. Product gap: no native broadcast/embed feature for intranet integration.

steps.description: Project communications lead/marketing identifies project as internal visibility candidate.
Evercam camera positions reviewed to identify best feeds for internal sharing.
Shared access link/embedded feed URL generated with appropriate access controls.
Live feed embedded in internal platform (SharePoint/Teams) or configured for video wall.
Recurring time-lapse export schedule established for regular internal updates.
At key milestones, snapshot/clip prepared and circulated with explanatory note.
Communications team monitors engagement and adjusts frequency/format.
At project completion, final highlight time-lapse produced and shared internally as celebration.

workflows.trigger: Project reaches stage of sufficient visual interest that contractor leadership/communications function decides to make site visible to broader organisation.
workflows.activity: Configuring and maintaining regular internal communications channel through which Evercam footage is distributed to internal staff.

evidence.quote: The contractor embedded a live Evercam feed from their largest active project into their SharePoint intranet homepage — describing it as "the first thing people see when they log on in the morning" and noting that it had generated more internal engagement than any other intranet content on record.

A live video wall in the contractor's head office reception displayed simultaneous feeds from six active projects — used both for internal staff awareness and as a business development asset when hosting client visits, with directors able to discuss live site progress in real time without leaving the building.

workflows.conclusion: Internal communications channel maintained for project duration. At completion, final time-lapse/highlight reel distributed as achievement celebration.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam live camera feeds and time-lapse videos embedded in corporate intranets (SharePoint), displayed on office video walls, or shared via communication platforms to give head office staff real-time site visibility.

workflows.name: Stakeholder & Owner Progress Reporting
workflows.notes: Structurally distinct from Workflow 1 (Remote Monitoring): this workflow is audience-facing and output-focused, producing a reporting artefact delivered to a non-operational stakeholder.

steps.description: A reporting trigger occurs — a scheduled reporting date arrives, a meeting is approaching, or an owner/investor requests a progress update.
PM or coordinator identifies the reporting audience and the format expected — live access, time-lapse export, snapshot summary, or video presentation.
For time-lapse delivery: the Evercam time-lapse generation tool produces a compressed video covering the relevant reporting period.
For live access delivery: view-only credentials or a shared link sent to the owner or investor for real-time or historical footage access at their convenience.
For meeting presentation: PM opens Evercam live view or plays a time-lapse during the OAC or board meeting, replacing static PowerPoint photographs.
For snapshot-based reporting: compare or snapshot tool generates before-and-after paired images at defined milestone intervals, exported as a PDF or image set.
Specific points of interest — structural milestones, concrete pours, topping-out events — highlighted within the footage with annotations or verbal commentary.
Audience questions about progress, sequencing, or site conditions answered directly by reference to footage — avoiding a site visit or additional report.
The reporting artefact (time-lapse video, snapshot set, or access link) shared with the audience post-meeting as a permanent record.
The process repeats on the next reporting cycle, with the time-lapse extending automatically from the last reporting date.

workflows.trigger: A scheduled reporting cycle, an upcoming OAC or board-level meeting, an investor draw-down inspection, or an ad-hoc owner request for a progress update.
workflows.activity: Assembling and delivering a visual progress update — time-lapse video, automated snapshot sequences, live camera access, or curated footage clips — to owners, investors, design team members, or senior management.

evidence.quote: The developer gives the time-lapse to the investor as part of the monthly draw-down reporting package — it shows the lender that the money is being spent and the building is going up.
He plays the Evercam time-lapse at every OAC meeting — it's become a standard agenda item. Clients love it and it saves 20 minutes of verbal progress updates.
We gave the owner a view-only login. They stopped calling us every week asking for photo updates. It's just there whenever they want to look.

workflows.conclusion: The reporting audience has received a clear, visual, credible account of site progress. Reporting obligation discharged and any questions answered visually without requiring a site visit.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam time-lapse videos, automated snapshot sequences, and direct camera access links replace the need to produce manual photographic progress reports or commission separate reporting deliverables.

Relevant camera(s), start date, and end date selected — defining the period to be compressed into the time-lapse.
Time-lapse speed, output resolution, and clip duration configured. TLP provides additional controls over frame selection and quality optimisation.
Where images from challenging conditions need to be filtered out (night frames, obscured lenses), frame selection tools used to improve output quality.

workflows.activity: Producing a complete, polished time-lapse video for distribution to investors, developers, government bodies, management boards, or the public as a standalone communication asset.

The project team is invited to board meetings for the hospital. They have used our time-lapse videos to provide progress updates.

workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam's Time-Lapse Creator and Time-Lapse Pro tools are the complete production system for this workflow — automatically compressing months of continuous camera footage into a polished, shareable time-lapse video.

workflows.name: Weekly Progress Meeting Preparation & Presentation
workflows.notes: Closely related to but distinct from Automated Progress Photo Distribution (Workflow 11) — Snapmail provides the raw image flow, but this workflow involves human curation and contextualisation for a specific meeting purpose.

steps.description: Weekly meeting cadence triggers preparation — typically 24–48 hours before the scheduled meeting.
PM or site manager reviews recent Evercam camera images and identifies the most informative views for each agenda item.
Compare tool used to generate before/after images for areas where progress needs to be demonstrated clearly.
A short time-lapse clip generated in Evercam's Time-Lapse Creator for the reporting period, or an existing weekly time-lapse accessed from the Media Hub.
Where 360° captures have been completed for the relevant period, the 360° walk is reviewed and key frames or a walk link prepared for sharing.
Visual assets (screenshots, Compare images, time-lapse clip, 360° link) assembled into the meeting presentation deck.
In meetings where participants have platform access, Evercam live view or Media Hub may be shared directly on-screen rather than via embedded slides.
During the meeting, PM presents the visual progress update alongside the written programme using Evercam images as the primary reference.
Attendees review visuals and raise questions, approvals, or concerns that inform programme and resource decisions.
Meeting minutes recorded; visual assets saved and linked to the meeting record for audit trail purposes.

workflows.trigger: A recurring weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly project meeting is scheduled, and the project manager must prepare a visual progress update to accompany the written programme and cost report.
workflows.activity: Selecting, assembling, and presenting visual evidence of site progress to give remote stakeholders, owners, architects, and senior management an accurate picture of current site status.

evidence.quote: Skanska USA uses a tiered approach — monthly meetings with the design team, bi-weekly meetings with owners, and internal marketing — all sourcing from the same Time-Lapse Pro video, assembled differently for each audience.
Project manager used Evercam's Compare tool to prepare before/after progress slides for a bi-weekly OAC meeting — the tool reduced meeting preparation time from two hours to approximately 20 minutes.

Site manager presented live Evercam camera views directly on-screen during a weekly progress meeting with a remote client, enabling the client to direct the camera PTZ to specific areas of interest in real time — turning the progress meeting into an interactive remote site walk.

workflows.conclusion: Meeting conducted with shared visual understanding of site progress. Decisions on programme, resource deployment, or RFI resolution made with current visual evidence.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam camera images, time-lapse clips, 360° walk documentation, and the Compare tool are used to prepare visual content embedded into weekly or OAC meeting decks.

QS/PM reviews claim and identifies inconsistencies with site observations.
QS/PM accesses Evercam platform and navigates to the relevant date range.
Live or recorded footage reviewed across relevant camera angles.
Snapshots taken from Evercam platform to capture work condition at claim date.
Where cloud resolution insufficient, higher-resolution local recording exported or 360° reviewed.
Visual evidence compared against claimed percentages.
QS prepares revised assessment/certification recommendation.
Adjusted certification communicated to subcontractor with footage references available.
Certified amount approved for payment or disputed with footage record available.

workflows.trigger: Subcontractor submits monthly pay application asserting percentage of work complete that the main contractor's QS believes may be overstated or inconsistent with recent observations.
workflows.activity: Reviewing Evercam recordings and snapshots from the claim period to establish a visual baseline of work actually completed.

evidence.quote: Visual verification of claimed work percentages via camera recordings used to support or challenge monthly payment applications — confirming the workflow's direct commercial application.
Cross-referencing site camera evidence against subcontractor valuations to establish whether claimed progress reflects actual site conditions at the time of the claim.
We manage to save €100k in contractor over charges.

workflows.name: Subcontractor Invoice & Payment Dispute Resolution
workflows.notes: Highest documented financial outcomes: €70k recovery (Monami Construction), €100k savings (Glenveagh), $35k direct cost saving (Barnhill).

steps.description: A subcontractor, supplier, or haulier submits an invoice or payment application containing claims the main contractor considers suspicious or unverifiable.
Main contractor's QS reviews the application and identifies specific line items, quantities, dates, or amounts that appear inconsistent with site records.
PM, QS, or site manager identifies the relevant cameras, Gate Report records, and time windows that would capture the work, delivery, or attendance being claimed.
Evercam recordings accessed and scrubbed to the relevant periods. Local HFR recording export requested if higher resolution is needed.
Gate Report ANPR data exported for the relevant period and cross-referenced with haulier or supplier claims.
Footage reviewed to verify or refute each disputed claim: worker presence, plant operating status, materials delivered, scope of work visibly completed.
Observations and discrepancies documented — specific timestamps, headcounts, vehicle counts, screenshots, short clip exports.
Footage clip or Gate Report export presented to the subcontractor or supplier — played directly from Evercam or shared digitally.
Subcontractor reviews evidence and typically withdraws, adjusts, or confirms the disputed element of the claim.
Adjusted payment processed and commercial record updated. Footage retained. Where subcontractor disputes the footage interpretation, matter escalated to adjudication.

workflows.trigger: A subcontractor, supplier, or haulier submits an invoice or payment application containing claims the main contractor's QS believes are inaccurate, duplicated, inflated, or relate to work not performed.
workflows.activity: Retrieving and reviewing Evercam footage and Gate Report records for the dates and locations relevant to the disputed claims — presenting that evidence to the subcontractor to resolve the dispute.

evidence.quote: Trevor brought the subby into his office and showed him a video of what happened (on Evercam), after which he returned the €70k. Trevor explained that if the video was not produced, the subby was willing to go to court.
We manage to save €100k in contractor overcharges.
evidence.source: Glenveagh — machine hire verified via Gate Report

evidence.quote: Subcontractors claimed that they had delivered tables to site. We were able to see that they did not deliver any tables.

workflows.conclusion: The invoice or payment application dispute is resolved. The main contractor pays only what is legitimately due. Court action or adjudication is avoided.
workflows.evercamRoleDescription: Evercam cloud recordings, local HFR recordings, and Gate Report ANPR data provide the primary independent evidence base for resolving billing disputes — verifying whether work was performed, materials delivered, quantities matched claims.

workflows.name: Subcontractor Labour & Attendance Verification
workflows.notes: Overlaps with Workflow 7 (Invoice & Payment Dispute Resolution) — this workflow focuses specifically on labour attendance and hours worked.

steps.description: A subcontractor submits a labour return, overtime claim, daywork sheet, or payment application containing specific attendance or hour claims.
Main contractor's QS, PM, or commercial manager identifies figures inconsistent with their site observations — specific dates, claimed hours, or worker counts that seem unlikely.
PM or QS identifies the relevant cameras and time windows (dates, start times, end times) that would cover the claimed worker attendance.
Evercam recordings accessed via the Recordings tab and scrubbed to the relevant arrival and departure windows.
Footage reviewed to observe: whether workers were on site at the claimed time; how many; when they arrived; when they left; whether they were actively working or idle.
Where Gate Report ANPR is deployed, vehicle entry/exit timestamps cross-referenced with labour claims to provide a second independent data point.

workflows.activity: Reviewing Evercam camera recordings and Gate Report data for relevant dates to establish actual mobilisation/utilisation/demobilisation timeline of specific plant items.

evidence.quote: We had a crane hire company claiming an extra week of standby charges — about £18,000. We pulled up the Gate Report and the camera footage and showed them the low-loader collecting the crane on the Tuesday afternoon. The invoice was withdrawn the same day.

Plant and equipment hire is one of the largest cost categories on civil engineering and structural construction projects. Day-rate and standby-rate disputes between main contractors and plant hire companies are extremely common — industry surveys consistently identify plant hire invoice disputes as among the top five sources of subcontractor payment conflict.

evidence.quote: The use of independent, timestamped evidence to resolve plant utilisation disputes is established practice in construction adjudication and arbitration. Evercam's combination of continuous camera recording and ANPR data provides a quality of evidence significantly more robust than site diary entries or plant logbooks, both of which are subject to challenge as self-serving records.
evidence.source: Industry standard — plant hire adjudication practice

workflows.conclusion: Plant utilisation dispute resolved — invoice confirmed and paid, or reduced to reflect verified utilisation period.

workflows.notes: Particularly relevant in North American markets where union labour agreements are prevalent on public sector projects. Product gap: Gate Report does not integrate with certified payroll systems.

steps.description: A union compliance obligation, contractual workforce requirement, or production rate discrepancy prompts a review of on-site labour composition.

Gate Report (ANPR) data cross-referenced with camera footage to reconcile vehicle entries with claimed crew sizes on certified payroll records.
Footage reviewed to observe crew composition — mix of trades present, any non-union workers on a union-mandated site.
Production rate benchmarking conducted where applicable — comparing observed output rates against rates claimed by the subcontractor.
Where a discrepancy found, relevant clips exported with timestamps and provided to the labour relations team or union representative.
Formal report or grievance response prepared, citing footage as corroborating evidence.
Compliance matter resolved — corrective action by the subcontractor, adjusted payment, or formal grievance outcome.
